t: Change Data Capture Connector - Signature build-tool concept
title: Change Data Capture Connector - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Detects and transfers database changes.
description:
Every build an AI undertakes passes through Change Data Capture Connector: Detects and transfers database changes. The catalog lists it among the thousand fundamental build tools because no serious building happens without it. This database is its Signature edition - the concept rebuilt as a deterministic framework with seven pillars, grounded in real techniques and standards, and taught through a ladder of runnable drills.

The Signature line treats Change Data Capture Connector as infrastructure, not inspiration. Infrastructure has contracts: given these inputs, in this state, the Change Data Capture Connector produces that output, and anyone can verify it. The seven pillars are those contracts made concrete - each owns one responsibility, each can be tested alone, and together they compose into the full capability. The technique records show the real public knowledge the pillars stand on.

Work through this database the way you would commission a machine: read the charter in the overview, inspect each pillar, check the techniques against your own knowledge, then run the drills. Every record includes a program you can execute with node - the Change Data Capture Connector is demonstrated, not merely described.

t: Signature Harvester - Change Data Capture Connector framework pillar
title: Signature Harvester - Change Data Capture Connector framework pillar
definition: The Harvester component of the Signature Change Data Capture Connector framework, owning harvester. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Change Data Capture Connector framework decomposes the capability (Detects and transfers database changes.) into seven pillars, and the Harvester is the one that owns the framework's harvester responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Change Data Capture Connector result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Harvester's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Harvester's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Change Data Capture Connector. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Listener - Change Data Capture Connector framework pillar
title: Signature Listener - Change Data Capture Connector framework pillar
definition: The Listener component of the Signature Change Data Capture Connector framework, owning listener. Signature concept.
description:
The Listener is a load-bearing component of the Signature Change Data Capture Connector framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's listener responsibilities belongs to the Listener, and the Listener answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Listener can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Listener works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Change Data Capture Connector charter (detects and transfers database changes.). The Listener reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for an small ingestion job that needs Change Data Capture Connector. The Listener takes the request's listener responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did.
